clue.text: Held back but given a second helping

definitions.meaning: kept in store or booked in advance, as a table set aside
read as ..., dished up once more

explanation.surface: Someone restrained in manner who nonetheless got seconds at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept back describes something booked or withheld, while the split reading means dished up again at the table.

clue.text: Celebrity about to present a key

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to put a case is to present it
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A famous person is about to perform in a certain key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as soon to, but 'about' is RE and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is fame or reputation, the standing a well-known person has.

clue.text: Sickly-looking swine taking everything in

indicators.note: the swine word takes in the other, holding it inside
completes taking in, the swine word enclosing the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
all means everything

explanation.surface: A pig that looks ill is gobbling up everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallow complexion is a sickly yellowish colour.

clue.text: Arrive at stretch of water

definitions.meaning: a straight length of a river

explanation.definitionFit: To get to a destination is to arrive, and a river's straight section between bends is a length of it.

clue.text: The prospect certainly troubles people

parts.note: prospect means a view, so this is an ugly sight that offends whoever looks at it

explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly building or sight that spoils the view.

clue.text: The robber is snapped and gets put inside

indicators.note: the word and is placed within the other piece

parts.note: a dog that snapped bit

explanation.surface: A thief has been photographed and then jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' suggests a camera, but here it is the past tense of bite, as a dog snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw who robs, typically on the road.

clue.text: Support for new law on lace-making

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Backing for fresh legislation on lace manufacture.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is money paid regularly to support someone.

clue.text: Not as others are, that's clear

explanation.definitionFit: Something different from the rest stands apart, and something plainly perceptible is sharp and well defined.

clue.text: Deter eccentric involving the restrained

indicators.note: the jumbled word wraps round the other
odd behaviour of the letters means they are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discourage an oddball who is dragging in the inhibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the first word into TERED before 'involving' wraps it round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up on a rope or chain, an animal is held back.

clue.text: Feels the head should be surrounded by friends

indicators.note: the head word goes inside the friends word, which encloses it

parts.note: pals are friends
the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone's head ought to be ringed by their mates.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpate is a medical term for examining by touch, so a doctor feels the body.

clue.text: The press wind up before time

indicators.note: the time letter follows the wind-up word

parts.note: to wind up a meeting is to close it

explanation.surface: Newspapers wrap up their business ahead of a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The press' looks like journalism, but a press is an old word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a large cupboard for linen or clothes, the same piece of furniture as a cupboard built into a wall.

clue.text: The male member is a dope!

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An insult that a male politician is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' reads as fool, but means cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is cannabis, and dope is slang for that drug.

clue.text: The MO's too put out to be pleasant

indicators.note: letters put out of their places are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical officer is too annoyed to be agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed, but it signals rearranging THE, MOS and TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means tasty or agreeable, usually of food, hence pleasing.

clue.text: Accorded little quarter, so quite pallid

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone shown no mercy goes very pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little quarter' reads as scant mercy, but it splits into WHIT (a jot) and E (a compass point).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very pallid has lost all colour, like chalk or snow.

clue.text: Overweight English lot!

parts.note: overweight means fat

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a crowd of overweight English people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot' looks like a group of people, but it means one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Your lot in life is your destiny, what fortune hands you.

clue.text: Taking a cake, could well be caned a lot

parts.note: a bun is a small sweet cake

indicators.note: signals that the word caned may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A schoolchild who took a cake might be beaten hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could well be' rearranges CANED into DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is plenty, a great quantity of something.

clue.text: General hankering for self-assurance?

parts.note: pan- is the prefix meaning general or all, as in pan-American
to ache for something is to hanker after it

explanation.surface: An army general longing for confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an officer, but it is the prefix pan-.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and style, a swaggering assurance.

clue.text: Hanging around some rich aunt in great hopes of irritating

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A legacy hunter stays near a wealthy aunt hoping for gain.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last letter of 'rich' and ends on the G of 'great'; 'hopes of irritating' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Haunting a place is frequenting it, loitering there persistently.

clue.text: Goes on producing soft toys for youngsters

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
rattles are babies' toys

explanation.surface: A shop that goes on making cuddly toys for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft toys' reads as teddies, but splits into P and RATTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter on at length about trivia.

clue.text: Giving frolicsome dog a run on the beach…

indicators.note: playful movement of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Letting a playful dog have a run on the sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the beach' paints the seaside, but means a ship stranded on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel run up on shore is stranded, beached in the old phrase for a ship stuck on land.

clue.text: Mr Bogarde's knife

definitions.meaning: the British film actor's first name

explanation.definitionFit: The actor Bogarde was a star of British film, and the weapon is a Highland dagger.

clue.text: … welcome run, say

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting, hail
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Continuing the beach scene: a welcome run for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie it to the previous clue's dog on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, to declare.

clue.text: Inane is, put another way, stupid

indicators.note: putting the letters a different way rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Inane is, phrased differently, simply foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means silly, like a donkey.

clue.text: Some fence retaining or turning over pledge

indicators.note: the fence word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: a pale is a stake forming part of a fence

indicators.note: means the word or is read backwards

explanation.surface: A handler of stolen goods keeping something back while flipping over a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' suggests a receiver of stolen goods, but a pale is a fence stake; 'turning over' makes RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is a prisoner's word of honour, a promise given for early release.

clue.text: The French in the party may be picked out

indicators.note: the French article goes inside the party word

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French members of a political party may be singled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Select means chosen, carefully picked.

clue.text: Like music observed

definitions.meaning: written in notes, as a score is

explanation.definitionFit: Music is set down in written symbols for pitch, and something remarked upon has been seen and commented on.

clue.text: Bring back military force favoured by the body politic

indicators.note: places the state beside the other pieces

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
in favour is in, as in the in crowd
the state is the organised political community

explanation.surface: Soldiers backed by the government are brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position.

clue.text: Use up the cash-send little money in

indicators.note: the coin letter goes inside the send word

parts.note: taken as written
P, a penny, is a small coin

explanation.surface: Spend the money: send a few pennies in.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend is to pay out money until it is gone.

clue.text: Found in the small lake-also far from water

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake
and means also

explanation.surface: Something discovered in a little lake that is also remote from water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradicts itself on purpose: a lake far from water.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland means away from the coast, in the interior of a country.

clue.text: So many staying in a Hebridean isle can be irritating

indicators.note: the so-many letters sit inside the island's name

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Lots of people holidaying on a Scottish island find it tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiree is a small island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast; 'staying in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means annoying or tedious.

clue.text: Note: refuse cuts

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale
ashes are the waste left by a fire

explanation.surface: A memo saying rubbish collections are being reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashes are deep wounds or slashes.

clue.text: Steadier maybe, yet most expeditious

indicators.note: signals that the letters might form another word if rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something steadier may also be the quickest.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiest means the quickest or most prompt.
